# Food hygiene (cooking, flies, carriers) (`food_hygiene`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: helped by contagion_theory, hand_hygiene, boiled_water, pasteurisation, refrigeration
- Core idea: Food carries disease when excrement reaches it on hands, flies or dirty water, and when germs multiply in it while it stands warm. Five rules cover most of it: wash hands and tools; keep raw meat and its juices away from cooked food; cook meat, eggs and reheated dishes until they are steaming hot all the way through; eat food soon after cooking or keep it cold or boiling hot, not lukewarm for hours; use clean water and wash or peel raw fruit and vegetables. Cover food and latrines against flies. A healthy-looking cook can carry typhoid for years, so nobody with diarrhoea handles food and cooks wash their hands above all others. Boil milk.
- Pitfalls:
  - Trusting smell and taste; dangerous food usually smells normal
  - Believing salt, spices, smoke or a splash of vinegar make spoiled meat safe
  - Keeping cooked food lukewarm overnight; reheating may leave toxins already formed in the food
  - Blaming the food itself (fruit, cucumbers, fish) for epidemics instead of what got onto it
- History: china: long-standing custom of eating food cooked and hot and drinking boiled water; a habit, not a theory; europe: 1820–1822 – Kerner describes sausage poisoning (botulism); 1888 Gaertner isolates a bacterium from a meat poisoning outbreak; 1895 van Ermengem finds the botulism bacterium; americas: 1898 – US Army Typhoid Board (Reed, Vaughan, Shakespeare) blames flies and soiled hands in camps; 1907 Soper traces household outbreaks to the healthy cook Mary Mallon
- Read:
  - World Health Organization, Five Keys to Safer Food Manual (2006)
  - George A. Soper, The work of a chronic typhoid germ distributor, Journal of the American Medical Association (1907)
  - Judith Walzer Leavitt, Typhoid Mary: Captive to the Public's Health (1996)
